## citaAggregate data, spring 2025 - Annoterad!

Ladda in data och räkna ut starttime för kiruna vår 2025

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr) # for data handling
library(tidyr)  # for datan handling
library(car) # for levene's test
library(lubridate) # for date handling
library(ggpubr)
library(ggplot2) # for plotting
library(getRad) # radar data
library(bioRad) # radar data handling
library(suntools) # Solar position
library(moonlit) # moon illumination
library(mblm) # Kendall
library(DHARMa) #checking residuals 
library(rstatix) # effect sizes
library(coin) # effect sizes

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(scipen=999)

# Set to local timezone for sunset/sunrise() to work properly and not get sunsets occurring on the wrong (UTC) date
tz = "UTC"

# Set location Kiruna (sekrn)
lat<-67.70875
lon<-20.61779
```

# Night length

```{r night length}
# Done per year to not get duplicate night of year (noy). Note location specific!

## 2025
# gör en dataframe med alla datum
dates2025<-as.data.frame(seq(as.POSIXct("2025-01-01"), as.POSIXct("2025-12-31"), by = "days"))
colnames(dates2025)<-"date" # döp om columnen

#Räkna ut nattlängd för varje datum
dates2025 %>%
  mutate(noy = noy(date, lat = lat, lon = lon)) %>% # lägg till column med natt nr
  rowwise() %>% # anger att efter detta titta bara på varje rad för sig
  mutate(sunrise = bioRad::sunrise(date, tz = tz, lon, lat))%>% # räkna ut och lägg till kolumn med soluppgång
  mutate(sunset = bioRad::sunset(date, tz = tz, lon, lat)) %>% # räkna ut och lägg till kolumn med solnedgång
  mutate(next_sunrise = bioRad::sunrise(date+86400, tz = tz, lon, lat))%>% # räkna ut och lägg till kolumn med nästa soluppgång
  mutate(night_length = as.numeric(interval(sunset, next_sunrise) / minutes(1)))->night_length_2025 # räkna ut och lägg till kolumn tiden från solnedgång till nästa soluppgång.

## 2024
# gör en dataframe med alla datum
dates2024<-as.data.frame(seq(as.POSIXct("2024-01-01"), as.POSIXct("2024-12-31"), by = "days"))
colnames(dates2024)<-"date"

#Räkna ut nattlängd för varje datum
dates2024 %>%
  mutate(noy = noy(date, lat = lat, lon = lon)) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(sunrise = bioRad::sunrise(date, tz = tz, lon, lat))%>%
  mutate(sunset = bioRad::sunset(date, tz = tz, lon, lat)) %>%
  mutate(next_sunrise = bioRad::sunrise(date+86400, tz = tz, lon, lat))%>% 
  mutate(night_length = as.numeric(interval(sunset, next_sunrise) / minutes(1)))->night_length_2024

## 2023
# gör en dataframe med alla datum
dates2023<-as.data.frame(seq(as.POSIXct("2023-01-01"), as.POSIXct("2023-12-31"), by = "days"))
colnames(dates2023)<-"date"

#Räkna ut nattlängd för varje datum
dates2023 %>%
  mutate(noy = noy(date, lat = lat, lon = lon)) %>% 
  rowwise() %>% 
  mutate(sunrise = bioRad::sunrise(date, tz = tz, lon, lat))%>%
  mutate(sunset = bioRad::sunset(date, tz = tz, lon, lat)) %>%
  mutate(next_sunrise = bioRad::sunrise(date+86400, tz = tz, lon, lat))%>% 
  mutate(night_length = as.numeric(interval(sunset, next_sunrise) / minutes(1)))->night_length_2023


```

# Kiruna

## Kiruna spring 2025

```{r sekrn spring 2025}
# ladda data
sekrn_2025spring <- read.csv(file= "sekrn_2025spring.csv", header=TRUE,stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# aggregera över höjd
sekrn_2025spring %>%
  filter(gap == 0) %>% # filtera bort data som inte är komplett
  mutate(mtr = (ff * 3.6 * dens / 5)) %>% # räkna ut MTR och lägg till som kolumn "MTR"
  mutate(datetime = as.POSIXct(datetime, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%OSZ", tz = "UTC")) %>% # gör kolumnen "datetime" till datumn format
  mutate(previous_sunset = bioRad::sunset(datetime-86400, tz = "UTC", radar_longitude, radar_latitude)) %>% 
  group_by(datetime) %>% # gruppera på tidpunkt för att summera alla höjder
      summarize(
          radar = radar[1]
        , mtr = sum(mtr)
        , sum_dens = sum(dens, na.rm = TRUE)
        , lat = radar_latitude[1]
        , lon = radar_longitude[1]
        , height_antenna = radar_height[1]
        , day = day[1]
        , sunrise = sunrise[1]
        , sunset = sunset[1] 
        , previous_sunset = previous_sunset[1]) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(noy = noy(datetime, lat = lat, lon = lon)) %>% # lägg till column med natt nr
  mutate(dmtr = mtr - lag(mtr)) %>% #räkna ut skillnaden i MTR till föregående
  mutate(pos_dmtr = dmtr > 0) %>% # gör en variabel som säger när skillnaden är positiv (TRUE)
  mutate(run = with(rle(pos_dmtr), rep(lengths >= 4 & values, lengths))) %>% #identifera "runs" av 4 eller mer positiva
  filter(run == TRUE) %>% #filtrera ut "runs"
  group_by(noy) %>%  # gruppera per natt nr
  slice(1) %>% # välj den första varje natt
  mutate(time_to_sunset =
    ifelse (hour(datetime)>12, 
      as.numeric(interval(sunset, datetime) / minutes(1)),
       as.numeric(interval(previous_sunset, datetime) / minutes(1))))-> sekrn_2025spring_time 
```

```{r night length spring 2025}
sekrn_2025spring_night <- merge(night_length_2025, sekrn_2025spring_time, by = "noy", all = FALSE)
```

## Kiruna spring 2023

```{r}
sekrn_2023spring <- read.csv(file= "sekrn_2023spring.csv", header=TRUE,stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

## These vpts's from aloft do not contain "sunset", "sunrise" and "day", so that is added below
sekrn_2023spring %>%
  filter(gap == 0) %>% 
  mutate(mtr = (ff * 3.6 * dens / 5)) %>% # räkna ut MTR och lägg till som kolumn "MTR"
  mutate(datetime = as.POSIXct(datetime, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS")) %>%
  group_by(datetime) %>%
      summarize(
          radar = radar[1]
        , mtr = sum(mtr)
        , sum_dens = sum(dens, na.rm = TRUE)
        , lat = radar_latitude[1]
        , lon = radar_longitude[1]
        , datetime = datetime[1])%>% 
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(sunset = bioRad::sunset(datetime, tz = "UTC", lon, lat)) %>%
  mutate(sunrise = bioRad::sunrise(datetime, tz = "UTC", lon, lat)) %>%
  mutate(day = if_else(datetime>sunrise & datetime<sunset, TRUE, FALSE, missing = TRUE)) %>% # note missing set to TRUE to account for midnight sun conditions, so won't work during winter
 # note missing set to TRUE to account for midnight sun conditions, so won't work during winter
  mutate(previous_sunset = bioRad::sunset(datetime-86400, tz = "UTC", lon, lat)) %>% 
  mutate(noy = noy(datetime, lat = lat, lon = lon)) %>% # lägg till column med natt nr
  mutate(dmtr = mtr - lag(mtr)) %>% #räkna ut skillnaden i MTR till föregående
  mutate(pos_dmtr = dmtr > 0) %>% # gör en variabel som säger när skillnaden är positiv (TRUE)
  mutate(run = with(rle(pos_dmtr), rep(lengths >= 4 & values, lengths))) %>% #identifera "runs" av 4 eller mer positiva
  filter(run == TRUE) %>% #filtrera ut "runs"
  group_by(noy) %>%  # gruppera per natt nr
  slice(1) %>% # välj den första varje natt
  mutate(time_to_sunset =
    ifelse (hour(datetime)>12, 
      as.numeric(interval(sunset, datetime) / minutes(1)),
       as.numeric(interval(previous_sunset, datetime) / minutes(1)))) ->sekrn_2023spring_time 

## Currently contains NAs in night/day sums. Some are ok (missing data), but some night NA's are due to midnight light.
```

```{r night length spring 2023}
sekrn_2023spring_night <- merge(night_length_2023, sekrn_2023spring_time, by = "noy", all = FALSE)
```

# Full table

```{r}
sekrn_2025spring %>%
  filter(datetime == 2025-05-01) -> sekrn_date
```

```{r plot starttimes}

plot(integrate_profile(as.vpts(sekrn_2025spring)), quantity = "mtr") #plotta med biorad funktion för vpts
abline(v=as.POSIXct(sekrn_2025spring_time$datetime), col = "red")

```

```{r spring summary}
spring_sum_night <- merge(sekaa_2023spring_night, merge(sekrn_2023spring_night, sekrn_2025spring_night, all = TRUE), all = TRUE)
```

```{r fall summary}
fall_sum_night <- merge(sekaa_2023fall_night, merge(sekrn_2024fall_night, sekrn_2023fall_night, all = TRUE), all = TRUE)
```

```{r seasons summary}
season_sum <- merge(spring_sum_night, fall_sum_night, all = TRUE) 

season_sum %>% 
  mutate(season =
           case_when(
             noy < 180 ~ "spring",
             .default = "fall"
           )
         )  %>%
  filter(time_to_sunset >= -60 & time_to_sunset <= night_length + 60 
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    solarpos = solarpos(
      cbind(lon, lat),
      as.POSIXct(datetime, tz = "UTC") # Behövde tydligen definieras
    )) %>%
  mutate(
    period = 
           case_when(
             solarpos[, 2] > 0 ~ "day",
             solarpos[, 2] > -6 &  solarpos[, 2] < 0 ~ "civil twilight",
             solarpos[, 2] > -12 &  solarpos[, 2] < -6 ~ "nautical twilight",
             solarpos[, 2] > -18 &  solarpos[, 2] < -12 ~ "astronomical twilight",
             .default = "night"
           )) -> all_seasons
```

```{r moonlight}
 illumination = calculateMoonlightIntensity(
      all_seasons$lat,
      all_seasons$lon,
      date = as.POSIXct(all_seasons$datetime, tz ="UTC"),
      e = 0.24) 
rename(illumination, datetime = date) -> illumination_new
 
merge(all_seasons, illumination_new, by = "datetime", all = TRUE) -> season_filter
```

## Seasonal comparison

```{r}
#Spring histogram
season_filter %>% 
  filter(season == "spring") -> spring_season
ggplot(data = spring_season, aes(x = time_to_sunset )) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  labs(title = "Histogram of departure time spring", x = "Departure time", y = "Count")

#Normality test
shapiro.test(spring_season$time_to_sunset)
#Not normal W = 0.71758, p-value = 0.00001268
```

```{r QQ-plot spring}
qqPlot(spring_season$time_to_sunset)
```

```{r}
#Fall histogram
season_filter %>% 
  filter(season == "fall") -> fall_season
ggplot(data = fall_season, aes(x = time_to_sunset )) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  labs(title = "Histogram of departure time fall", x = "Departure time", y = "Count")

#Normality test
shapiro.test(fall_season$time_to_sunset)
#Not normal W = 0.80697, p-value = 0.0000000001806
```

```{r QQ-plot fall}
qqPlot(fall_season$time_to_sunset)
```

```{r equal variances}
leveneTest(time_to_sunset ~ season, season_filter)
#Levene's Test for Homogeneity of Variance (center = median)
#       Df F value  Pr(>F)  
#group   1  3.4488 0.06558 .
#      129                  
#Equal variances can be assumed
```

```{r stats}
season_filter %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise( 
    mean = mean(time_to_sunset),
    sd = sd(time_to_sunset),
    median = median(time_to_sunset)
  ) %>%
ungroup()
#season  mean    sd
#  <chr>  <dbl> <dbl>
#1 fall    240.  299.
#2 spring  216.  559.
```

```{r wilcox test}
wilcox <- wilcox.test(fall_season$time_to_sunset, spring_season$time_to_sunset, paired = FALSE, var.equal = TRUE, alternative = "greater", conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
print(wilcox)

#Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction
#data:  spring_sum_night$time_to_sunset and fall_sum_night$time_to_sunset
#W = 917, p-value = 0.008499**
#alternative hypothesis: true location shift is less than 0
#Significant difference between seasons!
```

```{r effect size}
wilcox_effsize(data = season_filter, time_to_sunset~season)
```

## Departure time vs night length

```{r}
#Departure time histogram
ggplot(data = season_filter, aes(x = time_to_sunset )) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  labs(title = "Histogram of departure time", x = "Departure time", y = "Count")

#Normality test
shapiro.test(season_filter$time_to_sunset)
#W = 0.77594, p-value = 0.0000000004035
#Not normal
```

```{r}
#Night length histogram 
ggplot(data = season_filter, aes(x = night_length )) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  labs(title = "Histogram of night length", x = "Night length", y = "Count")

#Normality test
shapiro.test(season_filter$night_length)
#Not normal W = 0.97296, p-value = 0.01017
```

```{r plot}
ggplot(data = season_filter, aes(x = night_length, y = time_to_sunset)) + 
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Departure time vs night length", x = "Night length", y = "Departure time")
```

```{r linear regression}
lm_night <- lm(formula = time_to_sunset~night_length, data = season_filter)
qqPlot(lm_night)
```

```{r GAM}
gam <- gam(time_to_sunset ~ s(night_length), data = season_filter, method = )
summary(gam)

#Family: gaussian 
#Link function: identity 

#Formula:
#time_to_sunset ~ s(night_length)

#Parametric coefficients:
#            Estimate Std. Error t value        Pr(>|t|)    
#(Intercept)    235.8       30.1   7.834 0.0000000000016 ***
#---
#Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

#Approximate significance of smooth terms:
#                  edf Ref.df     F p-value   
#s(night_length) 2.323  2.929 4.265 0.00577 **
#---
#Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

#R-sq.(adj) =  0.0871   Deviance explained = 10.3%
#GCV = 1.2176e+05  Scale est. = 1.1867e+05  n = 131

#Departure time significantly depends on night length! However weak correlation.
```

```{r Kendall}
model.k = mblm(time_to_sunset ~ night_length,
               data = season_filter)

summary(model.k)
confint(model.k)
```

```{r spring}
model.k.spring = mblm(time_to_sunset ~ night_length,
               data = spring_season)

summary(model.k.spring)
confint(model.k.spring)
```

```{r}
model.k.fall = mblm(time_to_sunset ~ night_length,
               data = fall_season)

summary(model.k.fall)
confint(model.k.fall)
```

```{r plot GAM}
# Generate the random hp dataset for predictions
new_gam <- data.frame(night_length = seq(min(season_filter$night_length), max(season_filter$night_length), 
                                length.out = 100))
predictions <- predict(gam, newdata = new_gam, type = "response", 
                       se.fit = TRUE)

# Plot the data and the GAM fit
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = season_filter, aes(x = night_length, y = time_to_sunset)) +
  geom_line(data = data.frame(night_length = new_gam$night_length, time_to_sunset = predictions$fit), 
            aes(x = night_length, y = time_to_sunset), color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(data = data.frame(night_length = new_gam$night_length, fit = predictions$fit, 
                                se = predictions$se.fit), aes(x = night_length, 
                                ymin = fit - 1.96 * se, 
                                ymax = fit + 1.96 * se), alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(title = "GAM Fit for departure time vs. night length", 
       x = "Night length (min)", y = "Departure time (min)") +
  theme_minimal()
#Better fit than the Kendall, and a bit weak correlation. So, results probably not as significant as p shows
```

```{r plot kendall}
new_kendall <- data.frame(night_length = seq(min(season_filter$night_length), max(season_filter$night_length), 
                                length.out = 207))
predictions <- predict(model.k, newdata = new_kendall, type = "response", 
                       se.fit = TRUE)

# Plot the data and the kendall fit
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = season_filter, aes(x = night_length, y = time_to_sunset, color = season)) +
  geom_line(data = data.frame(night_length = new_kendall$night_length, time_to_sunset = predictions$fit), 
            aes(x = night_length, y = time_to_sunset), color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(data = data.frame(night_length = new_kendall$night_length, fit = predictions$fit, 
                                se = predictions$se.fit), aes(x = night_length, 
                                ymin = fit - 1.96 * se, 
                                ymax = fit + 1.96 * se), alpha = 0.3) +
  labs( 
       x = "Night length (min)", y = "Departure time after sunset (min)") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 16), strip.text = element_text(size = 20), legend.text = element_text(size = 13), legend.title = element_text(size = 16))
#Very weak correlation, so probably not as significant as the p shows
```

```{r}
new_kendall_fall <- data.frame(night_length = seq(min(season_filter$night_length), max(fall_season$night_length), 
                                length.out = 207))
predictions <- predict(model.k, newdata = new_kendall_fall, type = "response",

ggplot() +
```
